assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Wavelength
items.clue: The distance from one wave crest to the next.

items.label: Dark energy
items.clue: The name given to whatever is causing distant galaxies to recede ever faster.

items.label: Dark mass
items.clue: Matter whose presence is inferred from its effects but which is not understood.

questions.stem: Light from a distant galaxy is compared with light from the same element produced in a laboratory on Earth. What is observed about the light from the galaxy?

options.text: Its wavelength is longer than the laboratory value
Its wavelength is shorter than the value on Earth
It looks red instead of its normal colour
It has been reddened by dust on the way here

questions.explanation: Red-shift is an observed increase in the wavelength of light from most distant galaxies, so the galaxy's light arrives with a longer wavelength than the same light produced on Earth.

questions.stem: The light from galaxy B shows a bigger observed increase in wavelength than the light from galaxy A. What can be concluded about galaxy B?

options.text: It is moving faster, so it must be closer to us
It is further away than A and is moving faster
It is nearer than A and is moving more slowly
It is a larger and brighter galaxy than A

questions.explanation: The specification states that the further away the galaxies, the faster they are moving and the bigger the observed increase in wavelength.

questions.stem: The light from most distant galaxies shows red-shift. What does this observation provide evidence for?

options.text: That the galaxies fly out through existing space
That the Earth sits at the centre of the universe
That space itself, the universe, is expanding
That the distant galaxies are slowing down

questions.explanation: The specification states that the observed red-shift provides evidence that space itself (the universe) is expanding.

questions.stem: According to the Big Bang theory, what was the universe like at the very beginning?

options.text: A giant star that collapsed and then blew apart
A single giant star that exploded out into space
A large empty space that matter exploded into
A very small region, extremely hot and dense

questions.explanation: The specification states that the Big Bang theory suggests the universe began from a very small region that was extremely hot and dense.

questions.stem: What do observations of supernovae made since 1998 onwards suggest about distant galaxies?

options.text: They are gradually slowing as they recede
They are receding ever faster as time goes on
They will slow to a stop and then fall back
The nearest of them are receding fastest

questions.explanation: The specification states that since 1998 onwards, observations of supernovae suggest that distant galaxies are receding ever faster.

questions.stem: Every distant galaxy is observed to be receding, and the further away a galaxy is the faster it recedes. Why is this evidence that the universe is expanding?

options.text: Because the galaxies were thrown outwards through space
Because the Earth must be at the centre of it all
Because space between all the galaxies is stretching
Because nearer galaxies are moving away faster

questions.explanation: The change of each galaxy's speed with distance is what the specification names as evidence of an expanding universe: space itself grows, so more distant galaxies separate from us faster.

questions.stem: How does the observed red-shift provide evidence for the Big Bang model?

options.text: The stretched light is left over from the original explosion
It proves the Big Bang, so the theory can never be changed
The red colour shows the early universe was very hot
An expanding universe must once have been small and dense

questions.explanation: Red-shift shows the universe is expanding; running that expansion backwards leads to the very small, extremely hot and dense beginning the Big Bang theory suggests.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how scientists were able to use observations to arrive at the Big Bang theory?

options.text: A model was proposed to explain what was observed
Red-shift observations proved the theory to be true
Nobody saw the beginning, so the theory is untestable
The theory came from the 1998 supernova observations

questions.explanation: Scientists build a theory that accounts for the observations, such as red-shift, and keep testing that theory against further observations.

questions.stem: Which statement about dark mass and dark energy matches what the specification says?

options.text: They are fully explained by the Big Bang theory
They both name the same invisible material
They are examples of what is still not understood
The 1998 supernova results predicted them both

questions.explanation: The specification states that there is still much about the universe that is not understood, for example dark mass and dark energy.

questions.stem: The pattern of lines in the spectrum of a distant galaxy is compared with the pattern produced by the same element on Earth. What is observed?

options.text: The lines are shifted towards the blue end
The whole galaxy appears red rather than white
The lines are brighter and further apart
The lines are all shifted towards the red end

questions.explanation: Red-shift is seen as the whole pattern of lines from a known element appearing at longer wavelengths than the laboratory pattern.

questions.stem: Light from galaxies X, Y and Z is examined. X shows a small increase in wavelength, Y a medium increase and Z a large increase. Which galaxy is furthest away?

options.text: Z, because it shows the biggest increase
X, because it shows the smallest increase
Y, because its shift shows a medium-sized galaxy
X, because it has lost the most speed

questions.explanation: The bigger the observed increase in wavelength, the faster the galaxy is moving and the further away it is, so Z is the most distant of the three.

questions.stem: Observations of supernovae made since 1998 onwards changed what scientists say about the expansion of the universe. What does this show about scientific theories?

options.text: A theory becomes a fact once the evidence supports it
New observations can change an accepted theory
Theories about the distant past can never be tested
The older theory must have been an untested idea

questions.explanation: Scientists use observations to arrive at theories, and a theory such as the Big Bang is developed further when new evidence, such as the supernova observations, arrives.
